 Judgment

Challenging judgment and award dated 30.09.2011 passed by learned Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court and Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Saundatti, in MVC No.1726/2009, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Saundatti
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts as stated are that on 21.03.2009, when claimant Prakash S/o Hanamant Benakoppa was collecting firewood by side of road, a tempo trax bearing registration no.KA.24/3660 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against him on Munavalli-Kagadhal road.
In accident, he sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained disability.
3. Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against owner and insurer of tempo trax.
4. On service of notice, claim petition was contested.
Insurer contended that driver was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive transport vehicle.
5. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence claimant's father as PW1, eye witness as PW2 and Dr.Mahantesh M.Hooli, as PW3.
Exhibits P1 to P16 were marked.
On behalf of respondents, two witnesses were examined and Exhibits R1 to R4 were marked.

6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of tempo trax by its driver, claimant was insured with insurance company and claimant was entitled for Prakash S/O Hanamant Benakoppa vs Gurusangayya S/O Guirayya Hiremath on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139662302/
2 compensation.

sentences.text:
However, on ground that driver was not having transport endorsement, liability of insurer was discharged and owner was held liable to pay compensation assessed at Rs.1,28,700/-.
7.
Aggrieved by said award, claimant is in appeal.

8. Shri H.M.Dharigond, learned counsel appearing for claimant-appellant submitted that, dismissal of claim petition against insurer by tribunal on ground that driving licence of driver did not have transport endorsement was not justified in view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Mukund Dewangan vs Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., reported in 2017 (14) SCC 663.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., reported in 2017 (14) SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as quantum of compensation it was submitted that PW1 had stated that claimant was earning Rs.4,500/- per month.
However, tribunal considered notional annual income at Rs.15,000/-, which was grossly inadequate.
It was further submitted that award of compensation towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities, attendants and other incidental charges were inadequate.
It was further submitted that failure to award any compensation towards loss of income during layoff period was also erroneous.
On above grounds, sought for enhancement.
9. On other hand, Shri M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel for respondent-insurer while conceding legal position in view of decision in Mukund Dewangan (supra), would however oppose appeal for enhancement.
It was submitted that on over all consideration compensation awarded was just and proper and did not call for interference.

10. Heard learned counsel for both parties, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
11.

From above submission and since there is only claimant's appeal on liability, finding regarding liability as well as quantum of compensation, points that would arise for consideration are:
"1.

Whether finding of tribunal on liability calls for interference ?
2. Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for ?"

POINT NO.1:
12.

In view of decision in Mukund Dewangan's case (supra), dismissal of claim petition against insurer on ground that non- possession of transport endorsement when it is not in dispute that driver was holding driving licence to drive light motor vehicle (LMV) and vehicle involved was tempo trax, would not be justified.
Therefore, said finding requires to be set-aside.
Point no.1 is answered in affirmative.
It is held insurer is liable to pay compensation.

POINT NO.2:
13.
Insofar as monthly income, PW1 stated that claimant was earning Rs.4,500/- per month.
Without any justification, tribunal considered notional annual income at Rs.15,000/-.
PW3- Dr.Mahantesh Hooli, assessed limb disability at 35%.
Tribunal has considered disability at 11% and multiplier applicable would be '18'.
Thus, future loss of income would be as follows:

sentences.text: 14. Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.44,000/- towards medical expenses, which does not call for interference.
15. Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards attendance and other incidental expenses.
Considering duration of inpatient, it would be appropriate to enhance to Rs.10,000/-.

16. Since income is reassessed and normally fractures take about three months to heal, it would be appropriate to award sum of Rs.13,500/- (Rs.4,500/- X 3) towards loss of income during period of treatment.
17. Tribunal has awarded inadequate compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
It would be appropriate to award sum of Rs.30,000/- towards same.
18. Claimant has sustained compound fracture.
Therefore, award of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering would be inadequate.
It would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.

19. Thus, claimant would be entitled for total compensation as follows:-
Sl. Heads Amount no.
1. Pain and suffering 40,000/-
2.

Medical expenses 44,000/-
3. Loss of amenities 30,000/-
4. Attendants and other 10,000/-
 incidental expenses 5. Loss of earning during laid 13,500/-
 up period (Rs.4,500/- X 3)
6. Loss of future income 1,06,920/-
 Total= 2,44,420/-
Therefore, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

20. In result, I pass following:
ORDER a. Appeal is allowed in part with cost.
